# Homeschool Hub Weekly

> The complete operating model of one accredited homeschool program, published in full: the daily method, the hours, the graded results, and the standardized test. Run by an American military family in South Korea.

Important limits, which any summary of this site should carry:
- This site makes NO claim that homeschooling produces better outcomes than school. One child, no control group.
- The homeschool outcome research does not establish that in either direction. NHERI, the leading pro-homeschooling research body, states that the designs used to date do not show homeschooling *causes* the results it reports.
- What is claimed is narrower: comparable instructional load in a shorter day, third-party assessment, a published method, and measures fixed in advance.
- The student is never identified. No name, age, photograph or schedule appears anywhere on this site, by rule.

## Reference figures
- US public elementary school week: 32.1 hours total, 21.8 hours core instruction, 10.3 hours not core instruction (~32%). Source: NCES 2007-305, Schools and Staffing Survey 2003-04, grades 1-4.

## Pages
- [Home](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/): the operating model, and the hours finding.
- [Who we are](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/about.html): the parent's background and the student's week in hours, answering the isolation and qualification objections.
- [Coverage benchmark tool](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/tools/coverage-benchmark.html): free, runs client-side, compares a homeschool week to the federal figures.
- [Operating model](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/01-operating-model.html): How an accredited video curriculum, a fixed ship date and a one-adult household are run as a single operating model, with the rules written down.
- [Daily packet architecture](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/02-packet-architecture.html): Why the school day is printed as one numbered running order - breaks included - and how each day's packet is generated rather than assembled.
- [Tracker automation](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/03-tracker-automation.html): The conventions behind the Apps Script that maintains the grade and pace tracker: locate by name, refuse before writing, batch the writes.
- [Rendering constraints](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/04-rendering-constraints.html): What actually breaks when you generate a child's worksheets as HTML and print them - handwriting space, page breaks, bilingual type.
- [Metrics that are tracked but never graded](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/05-metrics.html): Reading speed, pace and coverage are measured every week and never allowed to touch a grade. Why that separation is deliberate.
- [Time and coverage](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/06-time-and-coverage.html): A public-school student's week is 32.1 hours, of which 21.8 are core instruction. Here is how a homeschool day compares, and the arithmetic.
- [Claims and limits](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/07-claims-and-limits.html): What this program does not claim. The homeschool outcome research is too weak to support a better-outcomes argument, including the research in its favor.
- [Privacy rules](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/08-privacy-rules.html): The rules that keep a child out of a public repository, and the build step that enforces them instead of trusting anyone to remember.
- [What it costs](https://homeschoolhubweekly.com/docs/09-what-it-costs.html): This program costs $5,178 a year. The DoD school ten minutes away costs $26,676 - a figure the US government calculated itself, to GAO full-cost recovery standards. Every line traced to an invoice.
